answer: This economy resists sybils by making emission a scarce-slot lottery, not one-key-one-share. To enter, an identity burns a non-refundable lotus ticket bound to a quartz proof: the hash of a seed-specific work trace plus its address. Before the draw, keys that share timing, n-gram overlap, or co-attestation graphs collapse into one ticket, so farms cannot buy more odds by minting aliases. Winners are audited at a random peer summit; a mismatch or copy slashes a time-locked bond and voids the ticket. Clones therefore pay linear burn and slash risk while still counting as one share.
